resources.string: Olive oil roasted salmon with broccoli

Salmon fillet 150g
Broccoli 200g
Extra virgin olive oil 1 tablespoon
Minced garlic, lemon juice, black pepper, to taste

Rub the salmon with olive oil, minced garlic and black pepper; let it rest for 10 minutes
Cut the broccoli into small florets, blanch in boiling water for 1 minute, then drain
Preheat the oven to 200℃ and roast the fish and broccoli on the same tray for 12–15 minutes
Drizzle with lemon juice before serving
Mediterranean mixed vegetable and chickpea salad

Cooked chickpeas 150g
Tomato 1
Cucumber half
Bell pepper half
Red onion a little
Olive oil 1 tablespoon
Lemon juice, parsley, black pepper, to taste

Wash the vegetables and dice them
Mix with the chickpeas
Drizzle with olive oil and lemon juice, sprinkle with parsley and black pepper
Chill for 10 minutes for better flavor
Turmeric and ginger quinoa rice

Quinoa 80g
Minced ginger 1 teaspoon
Turmeric powder 1/4 teaspoon
Olive oil 1 teaspoon
Black pepper, chopped scallion, to taste

Rinse the quinoa and cook it in water at a 1:2 ratio for 15 minutes
In another pan, sauté the minced ginger in olive oil until fragrant
Fold in the quinoa and turmeric powder and stir until even
Sprinkle with black pepper and chopped scallion (black pepper helps with curcumin absorption)
Walnut and flaxseed yogurt cup

Unsweetened yogurt 150g
Chopped walnuts 15g
Ground flaxseed 1 teaspoon
Blueberries or seasonal fruit 50g
Spoon the yogurt into a cup\nSprinkle with chopped walnuts and ground flaxseed\nTop with the fruit
White beans stewed with tomato and olive oil

Cooked white beans 200g
Tomato 2
Onion half
Garlic 2 cloves
Olive oil 1 tablespoon
Basil or parsley, a little salt, to taste

Sauté the onion and minced garlic in olive oil until soft
Add diced tomato and cook until it releases its juices
Add the white beans and simmer over low heat for 10 minutes
Sprinkle with herbs and season with a little salt
Vegetable egg pancake (less refined starch)

Eggs 2
Grated zucchini, grated carrot 50g each
Whole wheat flour 1 tablespoon
Olive oil a little

Grate the vegetables and squeeze out some of the water
Mix with the beaten eggs and whole wheat flour
Cook in a non-stick pan with a little oil over low heat until both sides are set
Cut into pieces and serve
Oat and pumpkin porridge

Rolled oats 40g
Pumpkin 150g
Water or low-fat milk 300ml
Cinnamon powder a little

Steam the pumpkin and mash it
Cook the oats in water for 5 minutes
Stir in the mashed pumpkin and cook for another 2 minutes
Sprinkle with a little cinnamon powder
Steamed cod with mashed carrot

Cod 150g
Carrot 150g
Ginger slices, scallion sections, to taste
Olive oil 1 teaspoon

Top the cod with ginger slices and scallion sections and steam over high heat for 8 minutes
Steam the carrot and mash it
Drizzle the fish with a little olive oil and the steaming juices
Serve with the mashed carrot
Chicken breast with fresh vegetables

Chicken breast 120g
Lettuce, tomato, cucumber, purple cabbage 250g total
Olive oil 1 teaspoon
Lemon juice, black pepper, to taste

Boil the chicken breast or cook it in an air fryer until done, then slice it
Wash the vegetables and tear them into bite-sized pieces
Combine and drizzle with olive oil and lemon juice
Sprinkle with black pepper and toss
Mixed bean and vegetable soup

Mixed beans (red beans / chickpeas / lentils) 80g
Tomato 1
Onion, celery, carrot 50g each
Herbs, black pepper, a little salt, to taste

Soak the beans in advance
Dice the vegetables and sauté them until fragrant
Add water and the beans and simmer over low heat for about 30 minutes
Season with a little salt and sprinkle with herbs
Anti-inflammatory
Gut-friendly
Calorie-controlled

Review: a Mediterranean diet may reduce inflammation and symptoms; a low-calorie diet and weight loss may help people who are overweight / obese; processed foods / saturated fat / refined sugar may make things worse
Systematic review: dietary evidence in AS is extremely limited and uncertain (mostly small-sample, single-arm studies)
Systematic review: evidence in axSpA is limited; ω-3 (PUFA) supplementation may be beneficial; spices such as ginger / turmeric have anti-inflammatory evidence
Cross-sectional study: low marine ω-3 intake is associated with higher disease activity; low dietary fiber density is associated with more severe inflammation
Review: eating more fiber helps maintain the gut environment; the low-starch diet mechanism exists but clinical evidence is limited; a low-fructose diet is a potential direction
Mechanistic review: gut microbiota and the HLA-B27 molecular mimicry hypothesis (explains \"why diet may be related to AS\")
Review: low-starch diet and Mediterranean diet are the two main directions; vitamin D and bone health

Patient organization practical guidance: ≥4 servings of vegetables + 2 servings of fruit every day; calcium about 700mg/day; ω-3 ≥2g/day; less salt and sugar, use more spices; the Mediterranean diet is a balanced pattern worth following; be wary of diet claims that can \"cure AS\"
Note: this direction is still being verified in randomized controlled trials and there is no conclusion yet

Reference recipes, not medical advice; diet cannot replace medication. The available evidence overall is limited (especially for ankylosing spondylitis); before changing your diet, please confirm with your rheumatologist or dietitian.
